items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: this has nothing to do with the current political regime. It has all to do with things that have actually gone on since the end of the Johnson administration.

ctx.x: Are you optimistic about the country addressing some of those things that you mentioned in the past?

I’m personally optimistic but I’m secretly cynical — not pessimistic, just cynical — in the sense that for so long de Tocqueville really had it right when he talked about some of the failings of our country, one of them being that we like to put our head in the sand whenever we confront a serious quote problem unquote that we tend to want to run away from it. And we want to renounce things that are American. We’re so busy inventing things and constructing things that we just do it and then walk away from it…

running around here today. But it’s just that there has been an undeniable drift to neglecting the real problems that exist in our country at the moment. Racism is an obvious one. Sexism and classism, those are obvious. But things that aren’t so obvious, you know, the denial of basic education to everybody, and it doesn’t matter whether you’ve coming from a public school district that has a lot of money or a public school district that doesn’t have very much money. I can tell you, and actually I don’t have to…
